courses.subject: BIOS

courses.description: Introduction to ecological processes at individual, population, and community levels that occur in plant, animal, and microbial taxa, and their relevance to current environmental problems.

courses.description: Students will apply scientific principles to human performance related to sport and movement across an array of topics (e.g., rehabilitation, exercise physiology, locomotion biomechanics, prosthetics).

courses.title: Integrative Genetics
courses.description: Rigorous in-depth integrated coverage of rules and molecular basis of inheritance, incorporating primary literature and capitalizing on excellent prior knowledge of fundamentals of biology.

courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level APPH 3755 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 3755 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 3755 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BMED 3100 Minimum Grade of D

courses.title: Ion Channels in Health and Disease
courses.description: We will examine the basic biophysical properties, structure-function relationships, physiological regulation, pathology and pharmacological manipulation of ion channels with heavy reliance on recent literature.

courses.title: Integrative Physiology
courses.description: This course will focus on the integrative mechanisms maintaining homeostasis. Interactions among the various systems and their plasticity and pathology will be emphasized.

courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 3380 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: Marine Ecology
courses.description: An overview of the physical forces and biotic interactions structuring marine communities and of the major threats to these communities.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 2300 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 2310 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 2335 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 2337 Minimum Grade of D

courses.description: Students will examine the ecological factors that affect dynamics, regulation, and evolution of natural populations, emphasizing the connections with mathematical models, genetics, and ecology.

courses.title: Human Pathology
courses.description: The course provides a comprehensive overview of clinical human anatomic pathology. The course will focus on select diseases and their etiologies, pathogenesis, morphological changes, and clinical manifestations.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 3753 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level APPH 3753 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 3753 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: Communicating Biological Research
courses.description: Students learn to convey the importance of research findings in the biological sciences and to critically evaluate research results through discussions and scientific presentations.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 4590 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 4690 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 4910 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 4690 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 4590 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 4691 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: Developmental Biology
courses.description: Investigation of cell differentiation and development, using the tools of molecular genetics and cell biology.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 2600 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 2610 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 2344 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 2354 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: Behavioral Biology
courses.description: An introduction to the study of the principles of behavior of all kinds of organisms, from microbes to mammals.
courses.prereqText: BIOS 1107L or BIOS 1207L or BIOS 1108L or BIOS 1208L.
courses.prereqGT: (Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1510 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1511 Minimum Grade of D or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1107 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1107L Minimum Grade of D) or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1207 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1207L Minimum Grade of D)) or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1520 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1521 Minimum Grade of D or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1108 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1108L Minimum Grade of D) or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1208 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1208L Minimum Grade of D))

courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: Evolutionary Developmental Biology – How to Build an Organism
courses.description: This course teaches students how the process of development from embryo to adult impacts evolutionary diversity and human health.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 3600 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 3600 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: Drug Discovery
courses.description: You will learn about the drug discovery process by identifying a disease and disease target, and then design a therapy to treat the disease.
courses.prereqGT: (Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 3450 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 3450 Minimum Grade of D) and (Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 4150 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 4150 Minimum Grade of D)

courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: Programming in Biological and Life Sciences
courses.description: This course introduces students to the basics of coding, applied to fundamental biological and medical questions.
courses.prereqGT: (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1107 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1207 Minimum Grade of D) and (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1107L Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1207L Minimum Grade of D)

courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: Epigenetics, Stem Cells, and Development
courses.description: This course will introduce the basic concepts and mechanisms in epigenetics, covering topics ranging from stem cell reprogramming, organismal development, social behaviors, to human diseases.
courses.prereqText: BIOL 2344 or BIOL 2354 or BIOL 3450 or BIOL 2800.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 2344 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 2354 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 3450 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 2800 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 3450 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: Community Ecology
courses.description: An advanced ecology course that covers classic and contemporary concepts, patterns, and processes in the field of community ecology.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 2335 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 2337 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 2300 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 2310 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: Health Genes Society
courses.description: Capstone project based investigation of the roles that genes and culture play in shaping health, including an introduction to personalized medicine.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1510 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1511 Minimum Grade of D or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1107 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1107L Minimum Grade of D) or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1207 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1207L Minimum Grade of D)

courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: Human Evolutionary Genomics
courses.description: An advanced course where students will discuss primary literature and use computational tools to investigate how evolution has shaped global patterns of human genetic variation.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1510 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1511 Minimum Grade of D or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1107 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1107L Minimum Grade of D) or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1207 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1207L Minimum Grade of D)

courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: Human Motor Control
courses.description: Course provides in-depth review of biomechanics and neurophysiology of human motion and discusses how human movements are planned, executed and corrected by the nervous system.
courses.prereqGT: (Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1520 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1521 Minimum Grade of D or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1108 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1108L Minimum Grade of D) or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1208 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1208L Minimum Grade of D)) or Undergraduate Semester level NEUR 2001 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: Genetics of Complex Human Traits and Diseases
courses.description: Introduction to the genetics and evolution of complex human traits, focusing on contemporary approaches to understanding susceptibility to malignant, metabolic, immune and psychological diseases.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 2344 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 2354 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 2600 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 2610 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: Origin of complex life: from cells to societies
courses.description: This course examines the evolutionary origins of complex life. We will examine the history of life on Earth and evolutionary process through which complexity arises.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1510 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1511 Minimum Grade of D or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1107 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1107L Minimum Grade of D) or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1207 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1207L Minimum Grade of D)

courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: RNA Biology and Biotechnology
courses.description: This course covers fundamental concepts of RNA biology as well as state-of-the-art biotechnologies that make use of RNA.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1510 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1511 Minimum Grade of D or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1107 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1107L Minimum Grade of D) or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1207 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1207L Minimum Grade of D)

courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: Chromosome Biology and Human Diseases
courses.description: This course explores the fundamental mechanisms governing metabolism of eukaryotic chromosomes and human diseases resulting from malfunctioning of chromosomal maintenance.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 2600 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 2610 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 2344 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 2354 Minimum Grade of D

courses.subject: BIOS
courses.title: Immunology
courses.description: A survey of modern immunology and its applications.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 2344 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 2354 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 2600 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 2610 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 3450 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 3450 Minimum Grade of D

courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1510 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1511 Minimum Grade of D or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1107 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1107L Minimum Grade of D) or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1207 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1207L Minimum Grade of D)

courses.prereqGT: (Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1510 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 1511 Minimum Grade of D or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1107 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1107L Minimum Grade of D) or (Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1207 Minimum Grade of D and Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 1207L Minimum Grade of D))

courses.title: Aquatic Chemical Ecology
courses.description: The course focuses on understanding the chemical mechanisms of aquatic signaling and the cascading effects on population regulation, community organization, and ecosystem function.
courses.prereqGT: Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 2300 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOS 2310 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 2335 Minimum Grade of D or Undergraduate Semester level BIOL 2337 Minimum Grade of D
